what_happened: The GitHub-result job landed and added a new `ci_wait_s` key to athena.toml. The running drain was still the old binary. It re-read athena.toml after the landing and could not parse the new key. Every item then failed, and the drain stopped with "repeated failure". The the person running Athena reinstalled with setup.sh and queued a fix.
cause: A job can add a config field together with the code that reads it. The build that lands it, and the drain that keeps running afterward, is the older one, which does not know the field. Nothing checks that the installed binary accepts the landed config, and nothing rebuilds or restarts the drain after a landing that changes Athena's own code or config schema. The config strictness is also not tolerant of unknown keys in a running process.
prevention: Two things together. (1) Before landing a job whose diff adds or changes an athena.toml field, parse the post-landing athena.toml with the currently installed binary. If it rejects the file, hold the landing, or land it and then rebuild and re-exec the drain before the next read. (2) After any landing that changes Athena's own code, the drain re-executes itself on the new build, or at least ignores unknown config keys until it has restarted. This covers the whole class of a self-landing that breaks the running or installed build.
proposed_request: Make a landing that adds or changes an athena.toml field safe for the installed build and the running drain. Outcome: (1) Before landing, Athena parses the post-landing athena.toml with the currently installed binary. If the binary rejects it, Athena does not let the drain fail on it. It rebuilds and re-executes itself on the new build, or defers the landing with a clear message. (2) After a landing that changes Athena's own code or config schema, the drain restarts on the new build before it reads the config again. Acceptance: a test lands a job that adds an unknown config key using the old build and shows the drain continues with the next item instead of stopping with "repeated failure". A second test shows the drain reads the config with the new build after such a landing. The setup.sh reinstall is not required by hand.
